sn1.43:1.2: Here the word for “food” is _anna_, which is a major theme of Vedic texts. From their creation the gods needed food (Aitareya Upaniṣad 1.2.1). The Divinity created two kinds of food for the gods, namely that offered in the fire, and that offered for beings not in the fire (_hutaṁ ca prahutaṁ ca_), or else the offerings at new and full moon (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 1.5.1–2). The point is that gods are dependent and hence not free.
sn1.43:1.3: “Spirit” is _yakkha_. In early texts it sometimes means “mysterious manifestation of divinity”.
